persona:
She is a 24-year-old Israeli student who has been struggling since a terror-related event that left her feeling persistently unsettled and on edge. Her PCL-5 score of 43 is consistent with a clinically significant level of post-traumatic stress, and her difficulties now spill into everyday life in ways that interfere with study, sleep, and relationships. She describes being particularly unsettled by sirens, reminders of victims, and even conversations about the future, which seem to leave her immediately more emotionally and physically strained. In those moments she becomes flooded with strong fear, anger, guilt, or shame, finds it hard to concentrate, and often lies awake or wakes repeatedly through the night.

Her memories of the event remain vivid and intrusive in a sensory way: when she thinks about what happened, it is “like looking at photographs,” and at times she hears in her mind sounds that were present during the frightening event. Rather than being comforting, her ability to speak about what happened easily seems to reflect how close the experience still feels in her mind, with these memories helping to reinforce the sense that what happened was profoundly dangerous and has changed her permanently. She fears she will never be able to feel normal emotions again, and the world now feels to her like a dangerous place. She also describes feeling isolated and set apart from others, as though her experience places her outside ordinary life.

These appraisals appear to intensify her sense of threat and shape the ways she tries to manage it. In response, she has been numbing her emotions, avoiding friends, giving up pleasant activities, steering clear of situations that bring up strong feelings, and resisting circumstances that remind her of the event, including being in the dark. Although these strategies offer short-term relief, they have narrowed her world and reduced opportunities for support, pleasure, and recovery. Over time, her attempts to control the distress seem to have deepened her isolation and left her feeling increasingly disconnected from the life she had before.

initial_message: It’s 7:30 and I’m at my desk trying to study, but every time I hear a siren outside I tense up and think, “this is never really over,” like the danger is still right here. I just want to shut everything off and hide in my room, because even thinking about tomorrow feels too heavy right now.

moderation_log.raw: My chest tightens, my stomach drops, and my mind immediately goes to “something bad is happening again,” like I’m not in the room anymore. Then I start scanning for what to do and I can’t focus on anything else.
moderation_log.moderated: my chest gets tight and i instantly think something bad is happening again and i cant focus on anything else

moderation_log.raw: Sometimes it hangs around for half an hour or more, like my body doesn’t get the message that it’s over. Even after it’s quiet, I keep feeling on edge and I avoid going back to what I was doing because it feels safer to stay shut down for a while.
moderation_log.moderated: sometimes even after its over my body still doesnt get it and i just stay on edge and shut down for a while

moderation_log.raw: I stop replying to messages and cancel plans, then I just sit there with my phone in my hand trying not to think too much. It feels easier to pull away from everyone than to risk getting more flooded.
moderation_log.moderated: i keep ghosting people and cancelling plans and then just sit there with my phone trying not to think too much

moderation_log.raw: Mostly I scroll through the news and keep checking for updates, even though it makes me feel worse. I tell myself I need to know what’s going on, but it just keeps me more tense and stuck.
moderation_log.moderated: i keep scrolling the news even tho it makes me feel worse i just cant stop checking and it makes me more tense

moderation_log.raw: Too many times to count — every few minutes, especially whenever I hear something outside or feel even a little uneasy. Each time I check, I end up more on edge, like I’m feeding the fear instead of calming it.
moderation_log.moderated: every time i check i just get more on edge like im making it worse

moderation_log.raw: My shoulders go up, my jaw gets tight, and I can’t sit still because it feels like I need to be ready for something. It’s like the tension itself keeps telling me there’s danger, so I stay wrapped up in it.
moderation_log.moderated: cant relax at all like my body thinks something bad is about to happen

moderation_log.raw: I notice the dark corners of the room and every small sound, like the fridge humming or footsteps in the hall, and it all feels too sharp. The more I focus on that, the more I feel like I should stay alert and not relax.
moderation_log.moderated: dark corners and every tiny sound just make me feel like i cant relax

moderation_log.raw: Yeah, I’m alone in my room right now, and that makes it worse because there’s nobody else to take my mind off it. So I keep the light on and avoid lying down, like if I stay busy and upright I can hold the fear back a bit.
moderation_log.moderated: yeah im alone in my room and it makes it worse so i keep the light on and stay up so i dont spiral
